cards.front: Which Act made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal, and who was the first to hold this post?
cards.back: Regulating Act of 1773. Lord Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.
cards.key_fact: Regulating Act 1773 created Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings).

cards.front: Under which British Act was the Supreme Court established at Fort William in Calcutta?
cards.back: Regulating Act of 1773 (established in 1774, comprising 1 Chief Justice and 3 other Judges). Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice.
cards.key_fact: Supreme Court at Calcutta established in 1774 under Regulating Act 1773.

cards.front: Which Act established the system of Double Government (Court of Directors for commercial, Board of Control for political affairs)?
cards.key_fact: Pitt's India Act 1784 established Double Government with Board of Control.

cards.front: Which Act completely ended the commercial monopoly of the East India Company, including tea and trade with China?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1833. It made the Company a purely administrative body.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1833 ended all commercial monopolies of the East India Company.

cards.front: Who was designated as the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833?
cards.back: Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1833 created Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck).

cards.front: Which Act introduced an open competition system for the selection and recruitment of civil servants (Macaulay Committee 1854)?
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1853 introduced open civil service competition (Macaulay Committee).

cards.front: Which Act is known as the Act for the Good Government of India, and what major title was created by it?
cards.back: Government of India Act 1858. It abolished the EIC and created the Viceroy of India (first Viceroy was Lord Canning).
cards.key_fact: GoI Act 1858 transferred power to the British Crown and created the office of Viceroy.

cards.front: Which Act introduced communal representation (separate electorates) for Muslims for the first time?
cards.back: Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms). Lord Minto came to be known as the Father of Communal Electorate.
cards.key_fact: 1909 Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

cards.front: Which Act introduced Dyarchy (dual governance: Transferred and Reserved subjects) at the provincial level?
cards.key_fact: GoI Act 1919 introduced Dyarchy in provinces and bicameralism at the centre.

cards.front: Which Act abolished provincial Dyarchy and introduced Provincial Autonomy, while proposing an All-India Federation?
cards.key_fact: GoI Act 1935 introduced Provincial Autonomy and divided powers into 3 lists.

cards.front: Under the Government of India Act 1935, where were the residuary legislative powers vested?
cards.back: In the Governor-General (Viceroy). Note: Under the Indian Constitution (Art 248), residuary powers are vested in Parliament.
cards.key_fact: Residuary powers in 1935 were with the Viceroy; in modern India they belong to Parliament.

cards.front: Who was elected as the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly in its first meeting on December 9, 1946?
cards.back: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, following the French practice of electing the oldest member.
cards.key_fact: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was temporary President on 9 Dec 1946.

cards.front: Who were elected as the permanent President and Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly on December 11, 1946?
cards.back: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President. H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari were elected Vice-Presidents.
cards.key_fact: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was permanent President; Assembly had two Vice-Presidents.

cards.front: Who was appointed as the Constitutional Advisor (Legal Advisor) to the Constituent Assembly?
cards.key_fact: Sir B.N. Rau prepared the initial draft as Constitutional Advisor.

cards.front: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee, and how many total members were in the committee?
cards.back: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was Chairman. The committee had a total of 7 members (set up 29 August 1947).
cards.key_fact: Drafting Committee had 7 members chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

cards.front: On what date was the Constitution adopted and enacted, and when did it come into full force?
cards.back: Adopted: 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day). Full commencement: 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).
cards.key_fact: Adopted 26 Nov 1949; commenced 26 Jan 1950 to commemorate Purna Swaraj Day (1930).

cards.front: What is the exact opening sequence of descriptors in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
cards.key_fact: Preamble keyword order: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.

cards.front: In which landmark case did the Supreme Court hold that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution and can be amended under Article 368 without altering the Basic Structure?
cards.back: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973). Overruled the 1960 Berubari Union case.
cards.key_fact: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) established Preamble is part of Constitution and subject to Basic Structure.
